mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed policy cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, p > 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a labor market softening without cost-push pressures, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening without inflationary spillover
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when the PAYEMS/CPIAUCSL interaction pattern persists.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 60% of INDPRO > 2% monthly up moves (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced near-term investment demand.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during two consecutive monthly HOUST declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased consumer confidence and investment inflows.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% after a 3-month decline
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE < 4.5% without prior decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates labor market strength without cost pressures, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market strengthening without inflationary spillover
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS/CPIAUCSL interaction is absent.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4% monthly decline in retail sales (not available in the catalog; fallback: use INDPRO for supply proxy) is not applicable here, so instead: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to supply-side contraction.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in 70% of 3-month INDPRO declines (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the monthly RSAFS (reserves) above 500 billion dollars indicates excess liquidity in the banking system, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return via equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when RSAFS remains below 500B for two consecutive months.
